summary:
## Idea
Game.Core SpatialGrid buckets point or bounds items by cell size, then filters regional/radius candidates. It remains the collision broad-phase implementation of record.

## Complexity
Build work/storage scales with inserted bucket memberships; a large bounds item can occupy many cells. Query cost is covered buckets plus candidate filtering, worst-case O(n) candidates.

## Use when
A bucket size fits a floating-point scene and local broad-phase queries dominate.

## Avoid when
A lockstep byte-equality promise or guaranteed logarithmic nearest queries are required.

## Pitfalls
Choose positive finite cell size; giant bounds/dense buckets defeat locality. Point and bounds builders/queries have different coverage contracts. Portable floating fields are not exact cross-runtime outputs.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Game.Core; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Game.Core.SpatialGrid.build: float -> seq<Point * 'T> -> SpatialGrid<'T>`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Game.Core
let empty: SpatialGrid<string> = SpatialGrid.build 16.0 Seq.empty
```

## Tests
SpatialGridTests is the cited existing query/property suite. Current Game compatibility profile grades SpatialGrid Portable.

## Bench
